term: immutable (ST I q.9; Lean parameter `Immutable` of `GodIsImmutable`)
definition: Altogether immutable means incapable of any change, not merely unchanging now (ST I q.9 a.1). The first argument excludes change because the first being has no potency, and whatever changes is in some way in potency. Stage 2 uses IsImmutable InPotency g := ∀ r, ¬ InPotency g r.
note: The case takes pure act, a sufficient condition in the first source argument, as its strong reading of altogether immutable. The source does not give a general biconditional identifying every use of immutability with this predicate. GodIsImmutable also permits an abstract Immutable parameter in the earlier group.
